svg.title: What the bot-health bot does when a bot fails
svg.desc: When a run of a bot or a scheduled workflow ends on the default branch, the bot-health bot looks at it; other runs of pull requests start nothing. When a bot of events, such as Welcome, or a workflow that keeps an issue of its own fails at its first attempt, also in a pull request or a fork, its last job starts the bot, which runs its failed jobs once more without an issue if Harden-Runner stopped one of them; otherwise it stays failed where that shows. A first failure that a second try can fix runs its failed jobs once more. A failure that stays opens one issue for the workflow, or updates it, with the failed jobs, their steps and their first errors. A run that passes closes the issue once every job that failed ran again in it and passed, in every leg of a matrix; a run that skipped such a job, or one without it, leaves the issue open. Every night, the bot looks at the latest run of every workflow, in case GitHub lost an event, but leaves a workflow that keeps an issue of its own to that issue. It starts a workflow whose schedule GitHub missed or switched off: one with no run of its schedule or by hand since the time of its schedule, whatever pushes ran it since.
